label: Rotational force from a held start
effort: Initiate a hip-led low kick without a bounce, preparatory dip or extra gathering step.
brief: A brief still start removes an immediate countermovement. The supporting jobs distinguish bilateral turn impulse, single-leg lateral drive, isolated hip-turn acceleration, free-thigh acceleration without toe push and release from a loaded stance.
marker: valid E2 attempts out of four per leg after a visibly still two-second start, with no redip and a controlled recoil.

e.name: Paused quarter-turn squat jump
e.execution: Hold a comfortable quarter squat for 2 s, then jump and turn up to 90 degrees without another dip. Use a two-foot landing already facing the new line and hold 2 s.
e.job: Produce rotational takeoff impulse without immediate dip assistance.
e.gate: Use a smaller turn instead for late orientation; a redip invalidates the held-start marker but counts as an attempt.
e.novelty: True held-start variant of Class 1 countermovement jump; the previously discarded paused candidate was never finalized as prior work.

e.name: Low roundhouse from a held split-squat start
e.execution: Kicking leg starts rear. Hold a shallow split squat 2 s, then drive through the front support leg into a low roundhouse, actively recoil and return to the original split stance. No initial bounce or deeper dip.
e.job: Link stance-leg force from stillness to the free thigh and pelvic turn.
e.gate: Make the starting squat shallower instead if rising produces a lurch; do not force a deep hold or fast knee lockout.
e.novelty: Held, lowered weight-bearing start changes force initiation compared with Classes 1–2 upright kicks.

e.name: Split-stance lateral jump to parallel landing
e.execution: From a shallow split stance with most weight on the named lead leg, push laterally away from that leg into a short flight; bring feet parallel for a two-foot stick. Face the same direction throughout; no scissor exchange.
e.job: Load asymmetrical lateral push while simplifying the receiving base to two feet.
e.gate: Shorten distance or reduce the rear-foot contribution; do not cross the legs in flight.
e.novelty: Asymmetrical split-stance lateral projection to parallel support, rather than a same-leg hop, opposite-leg bound or scissor switch.

e.name: Seated light-band hip-rotation acceleration
e.execution: Sit with thighs supported, hips/knees near 90 degrees and a very light loop at the lower shins. Start still, then move one foot a short distance outward briskly by rotating at the hip; knee/pelvis stay quiet. Return slowly; no bouncing or forced end range.
e.job: Give the hip internal rotators a small rapid force-expression task without the balance or whole-kick demand.
e.gate: Use self-resistance from the opposite hand instead if no suitable loop fits, or reduce range/tension for knee movement; speed is controlled, never a ballistic joint wrench.
e.novelty: New light, rapid isolated rotation task. P4 shares the joint action but uses challenging resistance and slow cycles; neither counts toward the other.

e.name: Rear-leg hover-start knee drive
e.execution: Stand on one leg with fingertip bench support. Hold the other toes just clear of the floor slightly behind the body for 2 s, then drive that bent knee forward/up briskly. Set it down under control before resetting; do not push off its toes.
e.job: Accelerate the free thigh from stillness without assistance from the swinging foot on the floor.
e.gate: Keep the hover close to neutral and chamber low; use a smaller path instead if the back arches or the support leg hops.
e.novelty: Removes the rear-foot push and starts the limb suspended, unlike the split-stance band drive or pre-chambered rotational sweep.

e.name: Lateral release step from held split stance
e.execution: Hold a shallow split stance for 2 s with the named leg in front. Push from that leg into one short lateral step, allow the feet/pelvis to open together up to 45 degrees, and finish in a stable kick stance. No jump or follow-on kick.
e.job: Release planted leg force into a grounded turn when there is no incoming momentum.
e.gate: Shorten the step and turn for foot sticking or overstriding; keep motion within 2 m.
e.novelty: Static loaded departure replaces Class 1 arriving lateral plant; the force source is a held front leg rather than an incoming step.

p_jobs: Maintain planted knee/hip extension with a smaller single working round while hip torque gets the main investment.
Preserve hip-extensor control of the stationary support leg.
Load the lateral hip range used in the held-stance release without a large adductor dose.
Primary strength investment: controlled hip internal-rotation torque from a still, supported setup.
Maintain active free-thigh lifting force without toe push or torso swing.
Preserve bent-knee ankle drive for rising from the stationary support stance.
s_jobs: Small supported airplane cycles prepare the hip to control a held base; foot holds reinforce quiet pressure before heel release.
readiness: The coach must see a still start and freely turning feet. E4 uses only a short comfortable hip arc and very light resistance; do not convert it into forceful knee/ankle rotation.
strength_reason: Compared with Class 2 [2,1,1,1,1,2], use [1,1,1,2,1,1]: 92 working reps instead of 96. This reallocates sets toward hip torque while reducing split-squat/calf work; it does not prescribe heavier bands or prove increased capacity.
exposure_note: Eight bilateral landings and no unilateral landings. Twenty efforts remain grounded, including eight kicks. The hover and still-start pauses add active time, not extra repetitions.
space: All starts and turns stay in a clear footprint; the lateral flight/step stays within 2 m plus 2 m recovery clearance in a 10 m lane. Bench dimensions and band fit need qualification.
progression: The preceding class addressed lead-leg release; this one changes the initiation condition to stillness and reduces landing count from twelve to eight. Keep angle and height controllable. No prior performance is assumed.
audit: A second seated or paused bilateral jump would duplicate the held-start job, so the other flight uses asymmetrical lateral push and a two-foot catch. Isolated rotation is four fast light efforts only; its slow strength counterpart gets relative load rather than speed. Forceful end-range rotation and maximum-height demands are excluded.
authoring_handoff: Review Class 3 and new feedback before Class 4, whose intended job is free-leg acceleration and active recoil; finalize and save it before continuing.
current_handoff: Record actual delivery/response and review the next saved class against readiness.
